title: Berlin Cemeteries - Quick Summary
items: **Five historic cemeteries, five different clocks.** Große Hamburger Straße has no gate at all. Dorotheenstadt and Alter St.-Matthäus-Kirchhof shift their closing time month by month, from 16:00 in midwinter to 20:00 from May to August. Invalidenfriedhof runs 07:00 to 19:00 from April to September and 09:00 to 16:00 from October to March.

**Weißensee is the one that catches people out.** It is closed all day Saturday for Shabbat, closed on public holidays, and shuts at 14:30 every Friday of the year. Men must cover their heads and kippot are lent at the entrance.

**Closest to the centre: Große Hamburger Straße**, about 11 minutes on foot from Alexanderplatz. Berlin's first Jewish cemetery, opened 1672, destroyed by the Gestapo in 1943. What is left is a lawn, a few recovered stones and a replica of Moses Mendelssohn's grave marker placed in 1990.

**Best short trip for famous names: Dorotheenstädtischer Friedhof**, about 16 minutes door to gate on the S-Bahn plus U6. Hegel, Fichte, Schinkel, Schadow, Rauch, Heinrich Mann, Anna Seghers and, under two plain field stones, Bertolt Brecht and Helene Weigel.

**Biggest by far: Jüdischer Friedhof Weißensee**, 40 hectares and nearly 116,000 graves, the largest preserved Jewish cemetery in Europe. Tram M4 runs there from Alexanderplatz with no changes. Allow at least 90 minutes inside.

**Where the Wall ran through the graves: Invalidenfriedhof.** More than 90 percent of its roughly 3,000 graves were cleared for the death strip after 1961, and a stretch of the border wall still stands along the canal.
